[LLEX.10.8.5] **`??` / `?` munch.** `??` (COALESCE) is a single token by longest-match
([LLEX.17.2]) — it out-munches a would-be `?` (NULLABLE). So `x::Int??d` lexes as
`x :: Int ?? d` and reduces as `(x::Int) ?? d` — a total cast then coalesce, with no
`NULLABLE` on `Int` ([LGRA.9.6], [LCST.4.1.3]). A fallible cast
that then coalesces must separate the target `?` from the `??`: `x::Int? ?? d` →
`(x::Int?) ?? d`. The implementation must verify all three: `x::Int??d` and `x::Int ?? d`
(the same token stream) → `(x::Int) ?? d`, and `x::Int? ?? d` → `(x::Int?) ?? d`.
